messages:
sara: heads-up — we're planning a controlled decommission of gpu-nodepool-west-2b tonight at 22:00 UTC. 2 nodes will be drained. asking for a quick run-through: any pods we should explicitly move or tolerations/affinity quirks we need to patch? :wave:

mike_sre: thanks for the heads-up. last drain we saw ~6 inference pods stuck Pending due to soft nodeAffinity + required toleration mismatch. might need a handback plan so they don't go into 'orphan' state. :eyes:

alex_ml: can you paste the taint we're using on gpu nodes? iirc we use: node.kubernetes.io/gpu=present:NoSchedule + custom redwood/gpu-isolation=exclusive:NoExecute for some pools. that second one caused evictions to be ignored by older tolerations.

jess_ops: correct — current taint on pool-west-2b: 
```
kubectl describe node node-xyz | grep -i taint
# node.k8s.amazonaws.com/gpu=true:NoSchedule
redwood/gpu-isolation=exclusive:NoExecute
```

cheng: the problem was some routing pods use preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity to prefer GPU nodes but don't tolerate NoExecute, so when we drain nodes they get stuck because CA can't place them back quickly and PDB blocks eviction. we should either add a temporary toleration or change affinity to preferred -> required fallback to cpu pool.

mike_sre: yep. quick options: 1) patch the Deployments to add toleration for redwood/gpu-isolation:NoExecute with operator Exists (short-lived), 2) drain with --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets --force (risky), or 3) pre-scale replicas to force rescheduling into CPU nodepool. i'd vote for (1) + a short rollout window.

sara: i prefer patching toleration for only services that are stateful or cannot restart quickly. for heavy inference workers we can allow a soft fallback to cpu by adding nodeAffinity with weight so CA can move them.

alex_ml: sample toleration patch we used last time: 
```
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      tolerations:
      - key: "redwood/gpu-isolation"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoExecute"
        tolerationSeconds: 120
```
this let pods stay alive for 2m during drain and allowed scheduler to reschedule onto other pools.

jess_ops: also watch CA configs — scaling down a GPU nodepool while CPU pool at limit will cause Pending. check cluster-autoscaler expander settings and max nodes for cpu pools. if cpu pool hit its max, nowhere to go. i opened a ticket to bump cpu-pool max temporarily.

k8s-bot: deploy hook: planned drain job queued for nodepool gpu-west-2b at 2026-03-18T22:00:00Z. Running pre-checks: PDBs, nodeConditions, PVC attachments.

mike_sre: pre-check results (quick): 3 Deployments have PDB with minAvailable=75%, one StatefulSet with local PVs (will block), 4 Deployments with preferred affinity only. recommendation: patch 4 Deployments tolerationSeconds=300, scale down stateful to 0 then resync PVCs, bump cpu-pool max by +3.

cheng: for the stateful we can do a warm-handoff: snapshot PVC, create short-lived CPU-backed pod to mount snapshot, ensure data access, then evict the GPU node. it's slower but safer.

sara: agree. operational plan: 
- 20:30 UTC: patch 4 deployments with short-lived toleration (tolerationSeconds=300)
- 20:40 UTC: bump cpu-pool max nodes +3 (io ok)
- 21:00 UTC: scale statefulset to 0 after snapshot
- 21:30 UTC: run drain on nodes with --delete-local-data --ignore-daemonsets (monitor)
- 22:00 UTC: decommission nodes
please ack if you're on-call for rollback/monitoring. :shipit:

alex_ml: ack. i'll watch inference error rates and model latency dashboards. i'll have a script ready to patch deployments back once done.

jess_ops: ack, i'll handle cpu-pool capacity change and watch CA logs. suggest we keep a quick kubectl one-liner to revert tolerations if something goes sideways.

mike_sre: one-liner to remove tolerations from all ns X deployments (example):
```
kubectl -n inference get deploy -l app=inference -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl patch -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":null}}}}' --type=merge
```
use with caution.

sara: good. i'll post a short announce to #infra-ops 30m before and update this thread when pre-checks done. thanks all.

deploy-bot: drain job started: nodepool/gpu-west-2b - nodes: 2. status: in-progress.

mike_sre: quick note: after last drain we saw scheduler event: 
```
Events:
  Type     Reason     Age                 From               Message
  ----     ------     ----                ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 3 node(s) had taint {redwood/gpu-isolation: NoExecute}, that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
so double-check the operator=Exists variant in patch to match older registries.

cheng: i'll be on standby for the stateful snapshot handoff. will also run a quick e2e to confirm fallbacks hit CPU pool properly.

sara: done for now — i'll update at 20:30 after toleration patch. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
